claims.note: Re-read at main 5440eeb: source line now cites the reproduced sweep and matches my numbers (Modern 0 of 4,000, Legacy 0 of 1,000, Ignore alone 30 of 30 and 10 of 10). Tours read at main 32f6219 (PR 54 merged); lab run at main 32f6219. Run on main 32f6219: both rounds emit ssh.kex.strict 'on' for client and server. Unit test A_peer_with_no_strict_marker_leaves_it_off passes (event says 'off'). I reproduced the sweep with a throwaway program (strict KEX switched off in a scratch copy): clear Ignore injected before the server KexInit, then the server's first encrypted packet dropped, then one more encrypted packet sent. Modern suite: 0 of 4,000 accepted (4,000 refused). Legacy suite: 0 of 1,000 accepted (1,000 refused); I stopped at 1,000 for time, so Jared's 4,000 is confirmed for Modern and Legacy is 1,000. Positive control, no attack: 200 of 200 accepted on each suite. Ignore injected and nothing deleted: refused 30 of 30 (Modern) and 10 of 10 (Legacy), so an injected Ignore does kill such a session. One nuance: every refusal came from the packet length check (SSH_PACKET_LENGTH), because the moved cipher stream garbles the encrypted length field before the MAC runs. The claim's reason, 'the MAC covers the plain text and a deleted packet moves the cipher stream', is right in its second half; suggest 'the length field is encrypted'. NVD names ChaCha20-Poly1305 and CBC with encrypt-then-MAC as the exposed modes; neither is in the lab. The names doc dates Jared's sweep 'before strict KEX', which the claim does not say.
